title: 08. GraphRAG: Knowledge Graph Construction
summary: Entity extraction is the process of identifying and classifying named entities (people, organisations, locations, products, concepts) in unstructured text — the first step in building a knowledge graph.

sections.title: ① Concept Explanation
sections.body: Entity extraction is the process of identifying and classifying **named entities** (people, organisations, locations, products, concepts) in unstructured text — the first step in building a knowledge graph. **Rule-based NER** uses pattern matching (regex, gazetteers); **statistical NER** (spaCy, Stanford NLP) uses trained sequence labellers; **LLM-based extraction** uses generative models to produce structured JSON output with richer context and better handling of domain-specific entities. In Graph RAG, entity quality directly determines graph quality — missed entities create disconnected graphs, over-extracted generic terms create hub nodes that degrade retrieval precision. The production best practice is a **hybrid pipeline**: fast spaCy NER for recall, LLM for precision and disambiguation, and a validation layer to filter noise.

sections.title: ④ Visual Explanation
sections.body:
```
                    KNOWLEDGE GRAPH CONSTRUCTION PIPELINE

  RAW CORPUS
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Doc1.pdf  Doc2.txt  Doc3.html  ...  Doc10M.json       │
  └─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        ▼ STAGE 1: PREPROCESSING
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Text Extraction → Coreference Resolution → Chunking   │
  │                                                        │
  │  "Apple hired Tim Cook"     → COREFERENCE →            │
  │  "Apple hired Tim Cook.      [Apple = Apple Inc.]      │
  │   He became CEO in 2011."   [He = Tim Cook]            │
  └─────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
                        ▼ STAGE 2: ENTITY EXTRACTION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                        │
  │  spaCy NER (fast, standard)   LLM Extraction (precise) │
  │  ┌──────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────┐   │
  │  │ PERSON: Tim Cook     │    │ PRODUCT: iPhone 14  │   │
  │  │ ORG: Apple Inc.      │    │ LAW: Section 230    │   │
  │  │ GPE: Cupertino       │    │ CONCEPT: edge AI    │   │
  │  └──────────────────────┘    └────────────────────┘   │
  │              │                        │                 │
  │              └──────────┬─────────────┘                │
  │                         ▼ MERGE + VALIDATE              │
  │                [Validated Entity List]                  │
  └─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼ STAGE 3: RELATIONSHIP EXTRACTION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Input: Entity pairs within same context window        │
  │                                                        │
  │  (Tim Cook, Apple Inc.) → EMPLOYED_BY [CEO, 2011-]    │
  │  (Apple Inc., iPhone 14) → PRODUCES                   │
  │  (Apple Inc., Google) → COMPETES_WITH                 │
  │                                                        │
  │  Methods:                                              │
  │  ┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌────────────────┐ │
  │  │Co-occurrence│ │  LLM-based   │ │Distant Superv. │ │
  │  │(weak signal)│ │(typed, rich) │ │(KB-aligned)    │ │
  │  └─────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └────────────────┘ │
  └─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼ STAGE 4: ENTITY RESOLUTION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  "Apple Inc" ──┐                                       │
  │  "Apple"    ───┼──► Canonical: "Apple Inc."            │
  │  "AAPL"     ──┘                                        │
  │                                                        │
  │  Resolution Methods:                                   │
  │  Rule-based → Fuzzy (Levenshtein) → Embedding →  LLM  │
  │  (fast)        (typos)              (semantics)  (amb) │
  └─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼ STAGE 5: GRAPH CONSTRUCTION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │         KNOWLEDGE GRAPH                                │
  │                                                        │
  │  [Tim Cook]──EMPLOYED_BY──►[Apple Inc.]                │
  │                                │                       │
  │                          PRODUCES                      │
  │                                │                       │
  │                           [iPhone 14]                  │
  │                                                        │
  │  [Apple Inc.]──COMPETES_WITH──►[Samsung]               │
  │  [Apple Inc.]──LOCATED_IN──►[Cupertino]               │
  └─────────────────────────┬──────────────────────────────┘
                            │
                            ▼ STAGE 6: COMMUNITY DETECTION + SUMMARISATION
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Leiden Algorithm partitions graph into communities:   │
  │                                                        │
  │  Community 1: [Apple, iPhone, iOS, App Store, Tim Cook]│
  │  Summary: "Apple Inc. technology ecosystem..."         │
  │                                                        │
  │  Community 2: [Samsung, Galaxy, Android, Seoul]        │
  │  Summary: "Samsung Electronics and mobile division..." │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

quiz.explanation: spaCy NER is fast (10k docs/min on CPU), cheap, deterministic, and great for standard entity types (PERSON, ORG, GPE). quiz.explanation: Distant supervision aligns an existing knowledge base (e.g., Wikidata, DBpedia) with raw text: if two entities are known to have a relationship in the KB, then any sentence mentioning both entities is assumed to express that relationship — generating training data automatically. It is used when you have a large corpus, a partial KB, and need to train a relationship extractor without manual labelling.
